what_happened: The job to give OLY-10-03 a mechanism, a later-task prevention check shown in athena status, was rejected at the final verdict. The verifier gave one major finding and no blockers. No acceptance criteria or checks are listed as failed. The finding: in later_similar_task (crates/athena-data/src/records/introspection.rs), the branch `landed.iter().any(|j| j > accepted)` counts any later landed job as a "similar task". The records already hold each job's class of work, so the check could have compared it. Status can therefore say a failure was "prevented" when no similar task came after the fix.
cause: The new status measure used a proxy, "any later landed job", in place of the real signal, a later job of the same class of work. Nothing required a new status measure to be run over the real records and compared with known cases before it counted as done. A predicate that is true for nearly every input passes tests built on hand-made fixtures, and only the verifier's independent reading exposed it. This is the same family of status-measure jobs for OLY-9-11 and OLY-10-02.
other_causes: The reading and criteria did not say what counts as a similar task, so the weak definition satisfied them.
The tests did not include a case where a later job is of a different class of work and must not count.
open_hypotheses: The input does not show whether the producer saw the class-of-work field in the records, or knew it was available.
The input does not show whether the reading defined 'similar' at all.
contradictions: Earlier cases in this class say a requirement to run the measure on real records would fix it, but this job was queued as one of that family before those rejections were known. It may not have had that rule available.
prevention: Add a check that every status measure has a test that runs it over the real job records. It must also have at least one known case that should come out true and one that should come out false, and the check fails when the measure gives the same answer for both. Here that means a later job of a different class of work must not count as a similar task.
proposed_request: Fix the later-task prevention check in athena status (OLY-10-03). A failure counts as "prevented" only when a later landed job of the same class of work exists, using the class of work already stored in each job's record. A later landed job of a different class must not count. Acceptance: (1) a test with records where a later job has the same class of work gives prevented; (2) a test where the later job has a different class of work gives not prevented; (3) a test where there is no later job gives not prevented; (4) the measure is run over the real records and the output is recorded in the changelog with one example of each outcome; (5) update the doc comment on later_similar_task; (6) cargo fmt --check, clippy --all-targets -D warnings and cargo test pass, including the existing tests that read athena status output; (7) add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
